patients.summary: High school teacher who joins in 2022 healthy, is diagnosed with IBS by GI in late 2024 with situational anxiety around a job change, and after her last practice visit in December 2025 self-refers to endocrinology for a suspicious thyroid nodule that proves to be papillary carcinoma. Total thyroidectomy in April 2026 is complicated by postprocedural hypoparathyroidism; the practice hears of it late, through a pharmacy call, the patient and a delayed surgical letter.

documents.title: New Patient Inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer primary care here; previous office in the Valley is cutting back hours and she wants easier access. Teaches high school, prefers summer or after 3:15 on school days. Membership info emailed. Booked new pt physical 8/17 at 9:00. Release of records form sent to her email, she will sign and send to her old office.

events.reason: new patient, establish care and physical

documents.title: New Patient Visit and Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Julie is a 42 y/o high school teacher establishing care. Coming from another primary care office; records release signed. Feels well. No complaints today, here mostly to have a doctor she can reach.

PMH: none ongoing.
PSH: C-section 2012, uncomplicated.
Meds: none.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: father with hypertension. Mother has osteoporosis. A maternal aunt was treated for papillary thyroid cancer.
Social: teaches high school, lives in Amherst. Has never smoked. Does not drink. Walks most evenings when the weather allows.
Gyn: Pap with HPV co-test last year at her old office, she says normal. Mammogram last fall, normal per her.

ROS: negative across systems; sleeping fine, energy good, bowels regular.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no adenopathy, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, low transverse scar healed. Extremities without edema. Skin clear. Mood good.

Assessment / plan:
1. Adult health maintenance. Screening bloodwork today (CBC, CMP, lipids), plus one-time hep C and HIV screens which she agreed to.
2. Tdap today, last one she thinks was with her pregnancy.
3. Old records requested; will reconcile her Pap and mammogram dates when they arrive. Next mammogram due this fall, order placed.
4. Flu and COVID this fall at a nurse visit.
Follow-up: annual, or sooner by message.

events.reason: records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Eighteen pages arrived from her previous primary care office. Reviewed and abstracted:
- Cervical cytology with HPV co-test, June 2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion; HPV not detected. Repeat interval 5 years noted by that office.
- Bilateral screening mammogram, October 2021: no suspicious findings, BI-RADS 1.
- Problem list there: none active. History of cesarean delivery.
- Medications: none.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Immunizations on file: COVID primary series spring 2021 plus booster, flu yearly.
Sent to PCP for sign-off.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Julie, all of last week's bloodwork came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Your old records came in too and line up with what you told me. Nothing to do until your mammogram this fall.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after school for vaccines. Afebrile, no current illness, no prior reactions. Influenza 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Bivalent COVID booster IM right deltoid. VIS reviewed. Observed 15 minutes, left feeling fine.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison with outside study of October 2021. The breasts are scattered fibroglandular density. No mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcification in either breast. Skin and nipples unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No mammographic evidence of malignancy. BI-RADS 1, negative. Annual screening recommended.

documents.title: Mammogram
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your mammogram from last week was normal. Next one in about a year; I'll put the order in at your physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam before the school year starts. Doing well. Summer was quiet, lots of walking. No new symptoms; sleeping and eating normally, bowels regular. Still on no daily medicines.

PHQ-2 negative.

Exam: vitals as recorded, weight unchanged from last year. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin without concerning lesions.

Plan: CBC and CMP this morning. Mammogram due again in the fall, order in. Pap/HPV next due 2026. Colon cancer screening starts at 45, next year. Flu and the new COVID shot when the fall supply comes in. See her next summer.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count and chemistry panel are normal. Have a good start to the year.

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks! First week with students is Tuesday, wish me luck.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu IM L arm and 2023-24 COVID IM R arm. Feeling well today, temp normal. Tolerated both. Out after 15 min.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with November 2022. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No new mass, distortion or suspicious calcifications. Axillary regions unremarkable.
